text:
alex: heads-up — since ~09:02 UTC we're seeing p95/p99 spikes on hosted API for text-gen. p95 jumped from ~180ms -> 1.2s, p99 to ~2.4s. No error rate increase, just tail latency. :rotating_light:
maya: saw it too in the dashboard. queue_depth metric for the serving pool spiked from 2->18 around the same time. any recent deploys? :eyes:
ron: small runtime tweak rolled at 08:55 — batching timeout bumped from 8ms -> 16ms to improve throughput. could be related.
jia: looking at request backlog logs. lots of short requests (seq len < 32) arriving in bursts from a single client-id. batch sizes shot up to 64 repeatedly.
emily: interesting — our kernel selector sometimes falls back to the generic kernel for short sequences if quantized kernels aren't chosen; fallback path is slower for small batches under heavy concurrency. profiling traces attached below.
alex: paste of relevant trace snippet:
```
trace_id=tr-00123 cpu_ms=45 gpu_ms=780 kernel=generic_attention seq=24 batch=64 kv_cache_hits=0
queue_depth=18 route=hosted-us-east-1 model=redwood-v1-small
```
ron: that kernel fallback happened ~08:56 when we hit a new model shard on node pool A. kernel decision logic uses heuristics (seq len distribution + quant config + hardware flags). bumping batch timeout increased opportunities for large batches of small seqs to form.
maya: that matches: p95 correlates with times where batch_size > 32 and queue_depth > 8. p50 unaffected.
jia: also seeing KV cache eviction churn. small requests had low cache reuse because requests are mostly different prefixes; eviction rate climbed 3x. KV misses -> more compute per request.
emily: what about noisy neighbor? node metrics show a single container spiked GPU memory & PCI traffic for ~3m before autoscaler moved loads. could be customer's long-running attention-heavy job spilling into hosting pool (dedicated isolation didn't catch it).
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-045 (latency spike hosted-us-east-1).
alex: immediate mitigations: 1) revert batching timeout to 8ms on runtime canary (ron). 2) add a temporary per-client burst limit for the noisy client-id (maya + jia). 3) increase KV cache per-shard budget on affected nodes by 15% (emily).
ron: reverting now on canary. rolling restart of runtime-canary-1..3 (kubectl rollout restart).
maya: I've applied a rate-limit rule: `rate_limit(client_id=xc-47, window=1s, burst=20)` — will monitor.
jia: collecting flamegraphs and per-request kernel selection logs to confirm fallback was the driver. will post artifacts here.
emily: quick perf regression note — kernel selector change from last month introduced a threshold tweak at seq<=32; that's probably the trigger when combined with the batching change. I'll open a PR to add a conservative override when queue_depth>10.
alex: timeline + owners: revert (ron) — in progress; throttling (maya) — done; KV bump (emily) — planning; follow-up PR (emily) and deeper profiling (jia).
ron: canary revert finished at 09:15 UTC; canary p95 back to ~220ms. rolling to rest of pool starting.
maya: rate-limit reduced incoming burst, backlog down to 3.
jia: uploaded profiling tarball to S3: s3://redwood-debug/INC-2026-045/profiles.tar.gz — contains kernel logs and flamegraphs.
emily: will tune kernel selector and KV budgets, target patch + test by EOD.
alex: thanks all. next steps: postmortem with timeline, root cause: interaction of batching timeout change + kernel selector threshold + noisy bursty client causing large small-sequence batches and KV churn. will coordinate postmortem draft.
maya: adding notes to incident board. :white_check_mark:
ron: reopening if any regressions after rollout.
(threads ends)
